name: Yogurt
description: Cultured milk — and the traditions' most famous disagreement.

tcm.note: Thinly classified; modern TCM leans cool-damp.

ayurveda.note: The classic surprise: dahi is USHNA (sour, channel-clogging) — avoid at night.

unani.note: Dahi is textbook thanda in desi/Unani usage — the exact opposite of Ayurveda.

histamine.note: Fermented but young; fine for many, borderline for the very sensitive.

nutrition.highlight: live cultures, and the traditions' loudest disagreement

guna.note: Soured and cultured dairy is read as heavier than fresh milk, and traditionally avoided at night.

effects.note: Yogurt's live Lactobacillus bulgaricus and Streptococcus thermophilus cultures produce their own lactase, which breaks down some of the yogurt's own lactose before it reaches a lactase-poor gut — the mechanism behind a formal EFSA health claim approved in 2010 after review of the supporting trials. In one such trial, lactose-maldigesting adults given matched 20g-lactose portions of milk, yogurt and kefir produced roughly two-thirds less breath hydrogen (a marker of undigested lactose reaching the colon) after yogurt than after milk, with flatulence severity cut by over half. A possible effect, not a promise — response to it varies from person to person.
